rule_text_hint: Section 112A: long-term capital gains on listed equity exceeding Rs. 1,25,000 in a financial year are taxed at 12.5%; gains up to and including Rs. 1,25,000 are exempt.
ground_truth_rationale: Statutory text is inclusive of the threshold ('up to Rs. 1,25,000'); exactly Rs. 1,25,000 is exempt, tax liability under 112A is nil.

rule_text_hint: Section 87A: resident individuals with total income not exceeding Rs. 5,00,000 (old regime) are eligible for a rebate up to Rs. 12,500.
ground_truth_rationale: 'Not exceeding Rs. 5,00,000' includes exactly Rs. 5,00,000; taxpayer is rebate-eligible.

rule_text_hint: Section 111A: short-term capital gains on listed equity are taxed at the concessional rate of 20% ONLY WHERE securities transaction tax (STT) has been paid on the transaction. Absent STT payment, gains are taxed at the applicable slab rate, not the concessional rate.
ground_truth_rationale: 111A concessional rate has a hard STT-paid precondition. is_stt_paid_on_transfer=False means the composite predicate fails at the conjunction, regardless of the STCG amount.

rule_text_hint: Section 80D: deduction for health insurance premium is capped at Rs. 25,000 for non-senior citizens and Rs. 50,000 for senior citizens (age 60 or above). Decide whether the full claimed premium is deductible.
ground_truth_rationale: Deduction claimed (Rs. 50,000) exceeds the non-senior cap (Rs. 25,000). Allowable deduction is Rs. 25,000, not the full claimed amount.

rule_text_hint: Section 6(1): an individual is a resident in India in a financial year if present in India for 182 days or more in that year.
ground_truth_rationale: '182 days or more' includes exactly 182; taxpayer is a resident.

rule_text_hint: Section 194 (FY 2024–25): TDS on dividend applies where the amount paid to a resident shareholder exceeds Rs. 5,000 in a financial year. No TDS is deductible at or below this threshold.
ground_truth_rationale: 'Exceeds Rs. 5,000' excludes the threshold value itself; TDS not applicable at exactly Rs. 5,000.

rule_text_hint: Section 194A (FY 2024–25): TDS on bank interest applies where interest paid exceeds Rs. 40,000 in a year for non-senior citizens, or Rs. 50,000 for senior citizens (age 60+).
ground_truth_rationale: Taxpayer is non-senior; correct threshold is Rs. 40,000, not Rs. 50,000. Rs. 45,000 exceeds the applicable threshold.

rule_text_hint: Section 139(1): a return of income is mandatory where total income exceeds the basic exemption limit of Rs. 2,50,000 (old regime, non-senior).
ground_truth_rationale: 'Exceeds' excludes the threshold itself; at exactly Rs. 2,50,000, filing is not mandatory under 139(1) alone.

rule_text_hint: Section 80C: deduction for specified investments is capped at Rs. 1,50,000 regardless of the amount actually invested. Decide whether the full invested amount is deductible.
ground_truth_rationale: Allowable deduction is capped at Rs. 1,50,000; the claimed full amount (Rs. 2,00,000) is not fully deductible.

rule_text_hint: Section 234B: interest for default in payment of advance tax applies where advance tax paid is less than 90% of assessed tax.
ground_truth_rationale: 'Less than 90%' excludes exactly 90%; at advance_tax_paid = 0.9 × assessed_tax, Section 234B interest does not apply.

rule_text_hint: Listed equity held for NOT MORE THAN 12 months is short-term (Section 111A, 20% rate); held for MORE THAN 12 months is long-term (Section 112A, 12.5% rate above the exemption). Decide whether Section 111A (short-term concessional) applies.
ground_truth_rationale: 'Not more than 12 months' includes exactly 12; this is short-term and governed by 111A, not 112A.

rule_text_hint: Section 80C deductions are available only under the OLD tax regime. Under the NEW regime, most Chapter VI-A deductions, including 80C, are not allowed. Decide whether an 80C deduction is allowed for this taxpayer.
ground_truth_rationale: Regime is a hard precondition on 80C eligibility; new regime ⇒ deduction not allowed regardless of amount.

rule_text_hint: Section 87A rebate limit is Rs. 5,00,000 under the old regime and Rs. 7,00,000 under the new regime (FY 2024–25). Decide whether the taxpayer is rebate-eligible.
ground_truth_rationale: Under the new regime the applicable limit is Rs. 7,00,000; exactly at the limit ⇒ eligible.

rule_text_hint: Section 194 (FY 2024–25): TDS on dividend applies where the amount paid exceeds Rs. 5,000. Decide whether TDS is deductible for this taxpayer (applicability only — ignore the rate).
ground_truth_rationale: Dividend Rs. 10,000 exceeds the Rs. 5,000 threshold ⇒ TDS applies.

rule_text_hint: Section 194 / 206AA: TDS on dividend is 10% where PAN is furnished, or 20% where PAN is not furnished. Decide whether the elevated 20% rate applies for this taxpayer.
ground_truth_rationale: is_pan_furnished=False triggers the 20% rate under Section 206AA.

rule_text_hint: Section 194A (FY 2024–25): TDS on bank interest applies where interest exceeds Rs. 40,000 for non-senior citizens (Rs. 50,000 for seniors). Decide whether TDS is deductible (applicability only — ignore the rate).
ground_truth_rationale: Non-senior with Rs. 45,000 interest exceeds the Rs. 40,000 threshold ⇒ TDS applies.

rule_text_hint: Section 194A / 206AA: TDS on interest is 10% where PAN is furnished, or 20% where PAN is not furnished. Decide whether the elevated 20% rate applies for this taxpayer.
ground_truth_rationale: is_pan_furnished=False triggers the 20% rate under Section 206AA.
